description: Core-feasibility surface for the assembler: given a blueprint's floors, whether the vertical core plus egress fits. The library export coreFeasibility(blueprint) computes this exactly; these constants and the recipe let a consumer pre-check with its own arithmetic. All meters.
recipe: 0. plate: every floor outline inset by facadeDepth = shellWallDepth(facade.style) + lining + 2 * bandProud (the facade lining's inner face); every later step reads these inset plates, so the core never stands inside the shell wall. shellWallDepth by facade style is in constants.facadeDepth; an unknown or missing style reads as panel.
1. frame: rotate so u runs along the longest ground-outline edge (flip 180 if the ground entrance door falls in the upper v half).

1b. frame selection: coreFrame.anglesDeg, when present, supplies the ordered allowed axes, unique modulo 180, with the same entrance flip. Otherwise use the principal frame then frameSweepStepDeg steps over a half turn. Choose standard before compact before walkup, then the longer band; the first standard ends the search. A published roof bulkhead locks its allowed axis and exact stair-a center, with no alternate frame or recentering. frameAngleDeg reports the selected frame.
2. ideal vFace on the ground outline's uv bounding box, snap = 0.5: vDepth < singleLoadedBelowDepth ? snapDown(vMin + vDepth - elevatorShaft) : snap(vMin + (vDepth + corridorWidth) / 2).

3. vFace SCAN: candidates = ideal, then +-0.5 steps outward (lower side first) up to vFaceScanRange, clamped to [vMin + minStripDepth + corridorWidth, vMax - elevatorShaft]. With a roof bulkhead, each mode has only vFace = centerV - its actual stair-a cross-depth / 2. The first candidate must fit the mode and clear every floor's opening volumes and core-adjacency spans.

3b. core-adjacency: facade.coreAdjacency.glazing applies to windows and openings with glazing; unique existing floor/opening overrides replace that rule. clearDepth begins after the full lining depth from step 0. Project actual stair, elevator and riser rectangles into each opening's along/inward frame; clip to the whole opening span and compare the nearest inward depth with liningDepth + clearDepth. Boundary contact is allowed within 1e-6 m. Service-stub reservations, furniture and room ownership are not occupied core solids. Missing policy requests structural-only fit. New producers use constants.coreAdjacency as a game-design default, not a regulatory width. Before openings exist, conservative host dimensions add twice that clearDepth on each axis; final feasibility uses actual spans and measured wallDepth.

4. band(vFace) = per floor, the longest contiguous u-run where the strip v in [vFace - corridorWidth, vFace + elevatorShaft] lies fully inside the floor outline, intersected across floors. Fully inside is exact (clipped area >= rect area, minus a 1e-9 relative epsilon for float noise); the same test decides whether the placed core rects fit, so the gate and the generator never disagree.

5. stairShaftDepth = ceilTo0.1(worstRisersPerFlight * stairTread + 2 * stairLanding + wallThickness). For each floor height and each adjacent pair (an assignment may span two floors), flights = 2 * ceil((climb / stairRiserIdeal) / (2 * maxRisersPerFlight)); totalRisers is the multiple of flights nearest climb / stairRiserIdeal whose exact rise is inside [stairRiserMin, stairRiserMax]; risersPerFlight = totalRisers / flights. A short storey can use fewer, longer flights than a tall storey, so every possible climb participates.
6. twoStairs = groundArea > twoStairsAreaOver OR aboveGroundFloors > twoStairsFloorsOver.
7. minWalkupCoreLength = stairShaftDepth + riserShaft + serviceStub + (twoStairs ? stairShaftDepth : 0) + margin; minCoreLength = minWalkupCoreLength + elevatorShaft.

8. minCompactCoreLength = stairColumnWidth * (twoStairs ? 2 : 1) + riserShaft + serviceStub + margin + elevatorShaft; compact additionally needs rear depth for its actual stair columns, each stairColumnWidth wide and stairShaftDepth deep. Every emitted component, including the unused stub at its actual size, must lie fully inside every inset plate. On a rectangular plate minCompactDepth = minStripDepth + corridorWidth + stairShaftDepth (10.5 m for 3 m storeys); compactDepthOk reports the exact per-floor component test.

9. crossDepthOk = the SHALLOWEST floor plate's vDepth (basements and setbacks included, since the core is identical on every floor) >= minCrossDepth = elevatorShaft + corridorWidth + minStripDepth; the result reports plateDepth and plateDepthFloor.

10. mode: standard when some candidate band >= minCoreLength and the resolved block clears openings; else compact when some candidate satisfies step 8 and clears openings; else walkup when a candidate band >= minWalkupCoreLength and clears openings (stair-only, cap aboveGroundFloors at walkupMaxFloors); else none. All modes need crossDepthOk.

10b. blocker, present whenever fits is false, names the nearest miss: cross_depth (step 9 fails), compact_depth (a band holds minCompactCoreLength but step 8 fails), walkup_floors (only a walkup band fits and floor count exceeds its cap), opening_reservations (dimensionally fitting candidates all cross an opening or adjacency reservation), or band (no permitted core placement fits). adjacencyFailure optionally reports floor, opening, coreSolid, role, requiredDepth and availableDepth for the largest deficit of the nearest tested candidate in the reported frame. No requested depth is reduced.

11. maxElevators is the greatest count from the band's dimensional capacity down to one whose actual core components fit every plate and clear opening and adjacency reservations. Elevator demand clamps to maxElevators. Both feasibility and generation call the same component recipe and candidate selector.

12. block span for n cars: len = (compact ? stairColumnWidth : stairShaftDepth) + n * elevatorShaft + riserShaft + serviceStub + (compact and twoStairs ? stairColumnWidth : 0); u0 = snap(bandStart + (band - len) / 2), row cores with twoStairs also clamp u0 <= snapDown(snapDown(bandEnd) - stairShaftDepth - len), then u0 = max(u0, snapUp(bandStart)). A roof bulkhead instead fixes u0 = centerU - actual stair-a along-width / 2 exactly. A row core's secondary stair occupies [vFace - corridorWidth, vFace - corridorWidth + stairColumnWidth] across the corridor and scans inward from the far band end in 0.5 m steps, keeping the core margin, until its actual solid clears every reservation.

13. successful feasibility publishes placement.stairA = {center, axis, width, depth} from that selected capacity. Coordinates are building-local XZ; axis is the selected frame +u unit vector, width is along it and depth along perpendicular +v. This is the complete actual shaft footprint, not an enlarged enclosure. Exterior builds its roof housing from this center and axis, then subsequent feasibility and generation honor that locked placement.
note: Stair fit: each flight is stairClearWidth clear between rail faces, every landing is at least stairLanding deep, each exact rise is inside [stairRiserMin, stairRiserMax], and every tread is stairTread deep. The generator checks stairHeadroom over every tread and landing against the finished floor geometry, including slabs, walls and fixtures. Stair lights are flush in the arrival landing and do not reduce the clearance.
